transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because the medical clinic for this logistics job I'm trying to get sent me. They wouldn't clear me for work. They told me my weight was too low. 

I don't really see it, to be honest. To me, I just look lean... you know, like someone who's ready to work and stay quick on his feet. But they said I had to come see someone, so here I am.
When you look in the mirror or think about your body, do you ever feel like you're overweight or worry about gaining weight?

Well, I don't really think I'm overweight, but... yeah, I definitely worry about gaining it. Like, if I eat rice or bread, or anything greasy, honestly, I just can't stop thinking about it. It feels like it's going to just sit on me right away. 

I usually end up checking the scale the next morning, or I'll see how my belt fits, just to make sure I didn't let myself go. I just need to keep things tight, you know?

Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food and feel like you can't stop, and if so, do you do anything afterward—like make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise intensely—to make up for it?

No, I don't really do anything like that. I don't... I don't lose control and eat a bunch of food all at once. It's actually the opposite for me. I just keep a tight lid on what I eat. So I don't ever need to make myself throw up or take pills or anything like that. I just stick to my routine and keep my portions small.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, so I can get a clearer picture of where you stand physically?

I don't have the exact numbers on me, to be honest. The clinic nurses took all that down for the physical, but I didn't really memorize it. 

I know how tall I've always been, but as far as the weight goes... I just step on the scale at home to make sure it's not going up. I don't really pay attention to the exact number, just that it's staying down where I want it. The clinic just told me it was too low to clear me for the freight job, and left it at that.
Would you be willing to check your phone, a recent form, or call the clinic to get your exact height and weight measurements from that physical, so we can calculate your BMI together?

I don't actually have any of the paperwork on me. And I never set up that... you know, that online patient portal thing on my phone that they always push, so I can't really look it up right now. 

I guess your office could call the clinic if you really need the exact numbers for your file. I don't mind if you do. I just know what they told me—that it was too low to clear me to go back on the freight line. But yeah, I don't have the exact measurements to give you right now.
Compared to your usual or highest adult weight, about how much weight have you lost, and over what period of time?

I'm not exactly sure what my highest weight ever was. I haven't really kept track of it over the years. I know I've lost a good amount of weight over the past, I don't know, maybe six or eight months? I just know my clothes are a lot looser now, and people have mentioned it. But I couldn't give you an exact number of pounds I've lost. I just know it's been a steady drop since I started being more careful about what I eat.
Even without exact numbers, can you give me your best estimate of your current weight right now, in pounds?

I honestly couldn't give you a good guess. Like I was saying, when I step on the scale at home, I'm just checking to see if the needle is lower than it was before. I... I don't actually look at the numbers on the dial. So I really don't know what it is in pounds right now.
Since you don't have the numbers, would it be alright if I have my office call the clinic directly to get your exact height and weight from that physical exam?
Yeah, that's fine. Like I said before, I don't mind if you call them to get the numbers for your file. You can go ahead and do that.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like feeling unusually cold all the time, dizziness or lightheadedness, thinning hair, or a lack of energy since you started losing weight?

I haven't really noticed any of that. I mean, I'm out moving freight all day, so I'm usually pretty warm. I haven't felt dizzy or had any issues with my hair thinning out. As for energy, I feel fine. I get through my shifts just like I always have. So, no, none of those things have been an issue.
Do you happen to have a weight listed on your driver's license or any other ID that might give us a more recent, official number?

Well, my driver's license has a weight on it, but... it's definitely not recent. They just carry over the same number every time I renew it, so it's from years ago. I haven't updated it in a long time, so it wouldn't really tell you what I weigh right now.
Did the clinic mention anything about your heart rate or blood pressure during that physical exam—like whether it was unusually low?

No, they didn't say anything about that. I mean, they did the usual checks—put the cuff on my arm, listened to my chest—but the doctor there didn't mention my blood pressure or heart rate being low or anything. If there was an issue with it, they didn't tell me.
Since we don't have a recent number, would you be willing to step on the scale here in my office right now so we can get an accurate current weight and height?
No, I... I really don't want to do that. I know you're just trying to get a number, but I'm not comfortable stepping on a scale right now. I'd rather not.
What pant or waist size do you wear now, and how does that compare to the size you used to wear before you started losing weight?

I'm not really sure about the exact numbers. I haven't bought new clothes in a long time. I just wear my usual work pants, and... well, I just have to pull my belt a lot tighter than I used to. They're definitely a lot looser on me now, but I couldn't tell you what my actual waist size is right now compared to back then.
Have you or people around you noticed your ribs, collarbones, or other bones becoming visibly more prominent as you've lost weight?

I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I don't spend a lot of time looking in the mirror without my shirt on. And nobody at work has said anything about my bones sticking out or looking different. So, no, I can't say I've noticed that.
Have you noticed any changes in your sex drive or sexual function since you started losing weight?

I haven't really noticed any changes, to be honest. I mean, my sex drive has always just been kind of normal for a guy my age, I guess. I haven't been paying much attention to that sort of thing lately, so I wouldn't say anything is different.
When the clinic told you your weight was too low to clear you for work, did they mention any specific number or BMI value at that time?

I don't really remember if they gave me an exact number. They might have mentioned something, but... I was mostly just frustrated that they wouldn't sign my paperwork. They just told me I was too light to pass the physical for the job. I didn't catch a BMI or anything like that.
You mentioned needing to tighten your belt—can you tell me how many notches or holes tighter you're wearing it now compared to before you started losing weight?

I guess I've moved it in about three or four notches. It's an old belt, so I had to actually poke a couple of new holes in it recently just to keep my pants up. But yeah, I haven't really kept track of exactly how many notches it's been since the beginning. Just enough so my clothes don't fall off while I'm working.
Can you tell me your current height—in feet and inches?
To be honest, I'm not exactly sure right down to the inch. I haven't actually had anyone measure my height in a really long time... so I don't have the exact feet and inches for you right now.
Do you ever feel like you need to exercise extra hard or for longer than usual specifically to make up for something you ate?

No, I don't really do that. I mean, my work is pretty physical as it is, moving stuff around all day. So... I don't go out of my way to exercise extra or anything just to make up for something I ate. I'm usually pretty beat after a shift anyway, so I don't really do any extra workouts.
Since seeing the number seems to be the issue, would you be willing to step on the scale here with the display turned away from you, so my nurse can record your weight without you having to see it?

I guess I could do that. If I don't have to look at the number, then... yeah, that's fine. I just really don't want to see it. But if your nurse just writes it down and doesn't tell me, I can step on the scale.
